names.name: Mango habanero
names.said: Sits near the top of a chain's heat ladder without being the top rung, which is usually something with a name like atomic.

text.what: A sweet-then-hot wing sauce: mango purée and corn syrup in front, habanero and cayenne behind. Orange, thick, and built to be tossed. It is the standard second-from-the-top rung on a chain wing board — hot enough to be a choice, sweet enough to finish.
text.story:
It belongs to the sauce-board era. As the market for chicken wings expanded, restaurants began creating and using a variety of sauces beyond Buffalo, some drawn from Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Caribbean and Indian cooking, and some invented as combinations — Blueberry BBQ Wing Sauce and Maple/Bacon Glaze among the examples — to hold customers' interest and grow the business.

Many bars and restaurants also build a deliberately extra-hot sauce for wing-eating challenges, and reward the people who finish with a photograph on the wall, a T-shirt, a free meal, or some combination.

*Inference —* mango habanero is the rung below that. It is where a board puts real heat that a table can still eat a whole basket of, which is why almost every chain carries a version and almost none of them publishes a number for it.
text.how: Toss, warm or cold — it is thick enough to cling without butter. Chains serve it on bone-in and boneless alike. A kitchen building its own reduces mango purée with vinegar and sugar and blends habanero in at the end, off the heat, because habanero's aroma cooks off before its heat does.
text.today: On chain boards nationally. As of 16 September 2026 the USDA label panel for Sweet Baby Ray's Mango Habanero Wing Sauce reads 100 mg sodium and 7 g sugar in a 1-tablespoon serving. Five chiles are named on that label — cayenne, habanero, chipotle, chili powder and chili de arbol — and no Scoville number is published for any of it, which is the pattern across this whole shelf.

confusable_with.tell: Fruit and corn syrup. Mango habanero leads with high fructose corn syrup and mango purée; sweet chili is water, sugar and pickled chilli.

ingredients: chili powder (chili pepper, spice, salt, garlic)
potassium sorbate and sodium benzoate and sodium metabisulfite (preservatives)
profile.note: Sweet Baby Ray's Mango Habanero Wing Sauce, 16 fl oz. Label serving is 1 Tbsp (18 mL), so the per-tablespoon figures are the label's own. pepper_rank 7 is aged cayenne red pepper, the first chile listed; the habanero the sauce is named for sits at 9, behind salt, and four more chiles follow it. The USDA transcription prints 'TOMATO PAST' at position 20 — read as tomato paste. Everything from rank 7 down is inside the 'contains less than 2% of' block, so the ranks there order the block, not the mass. No Scoville number, and no heat word on the front label beyond the flavour name.

recipes.note: Ingredients only, in label order, from the USDA branded-food panel. No method: a maker's process is not published and would not be free to copy if it were.
